<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="REPORT_INDEPENDENT_REGISTERED_PUBLIC_ACC">REPORT OF INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Shareholders and the Board of Directors of </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Randolph Bancorp, Inc. and Subsidiary</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Stoughton, Massachusetts</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Opinion on the Financial Statements</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of Randolph Bancorp, Inc. and Subsidiary (the "Company") as of December 31, 2020 and 2019, the related consolidated statements of operations, comprehensive income, changes in stockholders&#8217; equity, and cash flows for the years then ended, and the related notes (collectively referred to as the "financial statements"). In our opinion, the financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Company as of December 31, 2020 and 2019, and the results of its operations and its cash flows for each of the years then ended, in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Basis for Opinion</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">These financial statements are the responsibility of the Company's management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company's financial statements based on our audits. We are a public accounting firm registered with the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States) ("PCAOB") and are required to be independent with respect to the Company in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB. Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement, whether due to error or fraud. The Company is not required to have, nor were we engaged to perform, an audit of its internal control over financial reporting.&#160;&#160;As part of our audits we are required to obtain an understanding of internal control over financial reporting but not for the purpose of expressing an opinion on the effectiveness of the Company's internal control over financial reporting. Accordingly, we express no such opinion. </p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our audits included performing procedures to assess the risks of material misstatement of the financial statements, whether due to error or fraud, and performing procedures that respond to those risks. Such procedures included examining, on a test basis, evidence regarding the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. Our audits also included evaluating the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall presentation of the financial statements. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">/s/ Crowe LLP</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We have served as the Company's auditor since 2013.</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The accompanying notes are an integral part of these consolidated financial statements.</p>
<p style="margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-7</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Randolph Bancorp, Inc. and Subsidiary</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;" id="NOTES_TO_CONSOLIDATED_FINANCIAL_STATEME">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">December&#160;31, 2019 and 2018</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000342" name="us-gaap:BasisOfPresentationAndSignificantAccountingPoliciesTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000342_dcnt_06a69161-7d81-4199-a2d6-e5bd56b48f93">
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:4.54%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">1.</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:bold;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">BASIS OF PRESENTATION AND SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES</p></td></tr></table></div><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000364" name="us-gaap:NatureOfOperations" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000364_cnt_1">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Nature of Operations</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Randolph Bancorp, Inc. (the &#8220;Company&#8221;) is a bank holding company whose principal subsidiary is Envision Bank (the &#8220;Bank&#8221;). Envision Bank provides a variety of financial services to individuals and small businesses through its five branch offices in Massachusetts and seven loan production offices and lending centers located throughout Massachusetts and Southern New Hampshire.&#160;&#160;The Bank&#8217;s primary deposit products are checking, savings and term certificate accounts and its primary lending products are residential and commercial mortgage loans. The Bank is also actively involved in the sale and servicing of residential mortgage loans in the secondary market.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:continuation id="F_000364_cnt_1">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (&#8220;FDIC&#8221;) provides insurance coverage on all deposits up to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000433" name="us-gaap:TimeDeposits100000OrMore" contextRef="C_0001667161_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">250,000</ix:nonFraction> per depositor. As an FDIC insured institution, the Bank is subject to supervision, examination and regulation by the FDIC. Additionally, as a Massachusetts chartered savings bank, the Bank&#8217;s depositors are also insured by the Depositors Insurance Fund (&#8220;DIF&#8221;), a private industry-sponsored insurance company.&#160;&#160;The DIF insures bank deposits in excess of the FDIC insurance limits.</p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000366" name="us-gaap:BasisOfAccountingPolicyPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:8pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Basis of Presentation</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:6pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of Randolph Bancorp, Inc. (a Massachusetts corporation) and its wholly-owned subsidiary, Envision Bank (together, the &#8220;Company&#8221;). The Bank has subsidiaries involved in owning investment securities and foreclosed real estate and a subsidiary which provides loan closing services. All intercompany accounts and transactions have been eliminated in consolidation.</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:8pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The following significant accounting and reporting policies of the Company conform to U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;) and are used in preparing and presenting these consolidated financial statements.</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000367" name="us-gaap:UseOfEstimates" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Use of estimates</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In preparing consolidated financial statements in conformity with GAAP, management is required to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities as of the date of the consolidated balance sheet and reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting period.&#160;&#160;Actual results could differ from those estimates. </p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000368" name="us-gaap:CashAndCashEquivalentsPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cash and cash equivalents</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cash equivalents include amounts due from banks, federal funds sold on a daily basis and interest-bearing deposits with original maturities of <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000434" name="rndb:CashAndCashEquivalentMaturityPeriod" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">ninety days</ix:nonNumeric> or less.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000369" name="rndb:CertificatesOfDepositPolicyPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Certificates of deposit</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Certificates of deposit have original maturities ranging from one to <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000436" name="rndb:CertificatesOfDepositMaturityPeriod" contextRef="C_0001667161_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_20200101_20201231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">five years</ix:nonNumeric> and are carried at cost.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000370" name="us-gaap:FairValueMeasurementPolicyPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000370_dcnt_4cb62ef0-3254-4b8d-82bc-2a066bffd543">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Fair value hierarchy</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company groups its assets and liabilities that are measured at fair value in three levels based on the markets in which the assets and liabilities are traded and the reliability of the assumptions used to determine fair value.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Level 1 &#8211; Valuation is based on quoted prices in active markets for identical assets and liabilities.&#160;&#160;Valuations are obtained from readily available pricing sources.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Level 2 &#8211; Valuation is based on observable inputs other than Level 1 prices, such as quoted prices for similar assets and liabilities&#59; quoted prices in markets that are not active&#59; or other inputs that are observable or can be corroborated by observable market data for substantially the full term of the assets and liabilities.</p></ix:nonNumeric></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-8</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Randolph Bancorp, Inc. and Subsidiary</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (continued)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000342_dcnt_06a69161-7d81-4199-a2d6-e5bd56b48f93" continuedAt="F_000342_dcnt_41d2f904-2383-455e-939c-21c7eb864e2c"><ix:continuation id="F_000370_dcnt_4cb62ef0-3254-4b8d-82bc-2a066bffd543">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Level 3 &#8211; Valuation is based on unobservable inputs that are supported by little or no market activity and that are significant to the fair value of the assets and liabilities.&#160;&#160;Level 3 assets and liabilities include those for which the value is determined using unobservable inputs to pricing models, discounted cash flow methodologies, or similar techniques, as well as instruments for which the determination of fair value requires significant management judgment or estimation.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Transfers between levels are recognized at the end of a reporting period, if applicable.</p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000371" name="us-gaap:MarketableSecuritiesPolicy" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Securities</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">All securities are classified as available for sale and are recorded at fair value, with unrealized gains and losses excluded from earnings and reported in other comprehensive income/loss.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Purchase premiums and discounts are recognized in interest income using the level yield method over the terms of the securities.&#160;&#160;Anticipated prepayments on mortgage-backed securities are used in applying this method. Gains and losses on the sale of securities are recorded on the trade date and are determined using the specific identification method.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On a quarterly basis, the Company evaluates all securities with a decline in fair value below the amortized cost of the investment to determine whether or not the impairment is deemed to be other than temporary (&#8220;OTTI&#8221;).</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">OTTI is required to be recognized: (1) if the Company intends to sell the security&#59; (2) if it is &#8220;more likely than not&#8221; that the Company will be required to sell the security before recovery of its amortized cost basis&#59; or (3) for debt securities, if the present value of expected cash flows is not sufficient to recover the entire amortized cost basis. For all impaired debt securities that the Company intends to sell, or more likely than not will be required to sell, the full amount of the decline in fair value is recognized as OTTI through earnings.&#160;&#160;For all other impaired debt securities, credit-related OTTI is recognized through earnings and non-credit related OTTI is recognized in other comprehensive income/loss, net of applicable taxes. Because the Company&#8217;s assessments are based on available factual information as well as subjective information, the determination as to whether an OTTI exists and, if so, the amount of impairment, is subjective and, therefore, the timing and amount of OTTI constitute material estimates that are subject to significant change.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000372" name="rndb:InvestmentInFederalHomeLoanBankStockPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Federal Home Loan Bank of Boston stock</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Bank, as a member of the Federal Home Loan Bank of Boston (&#8220;FHLBB&#8221;), is required to maintain an investment in capital stock of the FHLBB.&#160;&#160;Based on redemption provisions of the FHLBB, the stock has no quoted market value and is carried at cost. The Company periodically evaluates for impairment based on ultimate recovery of its cost basis in the FHLBB stock.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000373" name="us-gaap:FinanceLoanAndLeaseReceivablesHeldForSalePolicy" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:8pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Loans held for sale and related derivatives</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:6pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The origination of residential mortgage loans is an integral part of the Company&#8217;s business. The Company generally sells its originations of such loans in the secondary market to either government-sponsored enterprises (&#8220;GSEs&#8221;) or other financial institutions. The servicing of loans sold to GSEs is generally retained while loans sold to other financial institutions are generally done on a servicing released basis. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Bank utilizes the fair value option pursuant to Accounting Standards Codification (&#8220;ASC&#8221;) 825, &#8220;Financial Instruments&#8221; for its residential mortgage loans being held for sale. Fair value is determined based on either commitments in effect from investors or prevailing market price and include the value of mortgage servicing rights. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Gains and losses on the sales of loans are determined using the specific identification method. In determining the amount of the gain or loss the Company takes into consideration the direct costs of originating the loan. Also included in the net gain on loan origination and sale activities presented in the accompanying statements of operations are fair value adjustments for mortgage banking derivatives (interest rate lock commitments with borrowers, and forward loan sale commitments with investors for the delivery of mortgage loans to third party investors including To Be Announced securities (&#8220;TBAs&#8221;)) and loans held for sale.</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-9</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Randolph Bancorp, Inc. and Subsidiary</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (continued)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000342_dcnt_41d2f904-2383-455e-939c-21c7eb864e2c" continuedAt="F_000342_dcnt_8f2e6828-f0f9-46e1-ae52-f0bd8ed02641">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000374" name="us-gaap:FinanceLoansAndLeasesReceivablePolicy" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Loans</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company grants residential real estate, commercial real estate, construction, commercial and consumer loans to customers.&#160;&#160;A substantial portion of the loan portfolio is represented by mortgage loans in Massachusetts and Rhode Island.&#160;&#160;The ability of the Company&#8217;s borrowers to honor their contracts is affected by real estate values and general economic conditions in these markets.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Loans that management has the intent and ability to hold for the foreseeable future or until maturity or pay-off are reported at their outstanding unpaid principal balances adjusted for charge-offs, the allowance for loan losses, and net deferred loan origination fees and costs and purchase premiums.&#160;&#160;Interest income is accrued on the unpaid principal balance.&#160;&#160;Certain direct loan origination costs and purchase premiums, net of origination fees, are deferred and recognized in interest income using the level yield method without anticipating prepayments.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Interest is not accrued on loans which are ninety days or more past due, or when, in the judgment of management, the collectability of the principal or interest becomes doubtful.&#160;&#160;Past due status is based on contractual terms of the loan.&#160;&#160;Interest income previously accrued on such loans is reversed against current period earnings.&#160;&#160;Loans are returned to accrual status when all principal and interest amounts contractually due are brought current and future payments are reasonably assured.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company periodically may agree to modify the contractual terms of loans.&#160;&#160;When a loan is modified and a concession is made to a borrower experiencing financial difficulty, the modification is considered a troubled debt restructuring (&#8220;TDR&#8221;).&#160;&#160;All TDRs are initially classified as impaired and placed on nonaccrual status. Generally, a nonaccrual loan that is restructured remains on nonaccrual for a period of six months to demonstrate that the borrower can meet the restructured terms. If the borrower&#8217;s ability to meet the revised terms is not reasonably assured, the loan remains on nonaccrual status.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000375" name="us-gaap:LoansAndLeasesReceivableAllowanceForLoanLossesPolicy" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000375_dcnt_e15dbb08-8b25-4d7e-adbd-21609283c08f">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.54%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Allowance for loan losses</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The allowance for loan losses is a valuation allowance for probable incurred credit losses.&#160;&#160;Loan losses are charged against the allowance when management believes the uncollectibility of a loan balance is confirmed.&#160;&#160;Subsequent recoveries, if any, are credited to the allowance.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The allowance for loan losses is evaluated on a regular basis and is based upon management&#8217;s periodic review of the collectibility of the loans in light of historical experience, the nature and volume of the loan portfolio, adverse situations that may affect the borrower&#8217;s ability to repay, estimated value of any underlying collateral and prevailing economic conditions.&#160;&#160;This evaluation is inherently subjective as it requires estimates that are susceptible to significant revision as either additional information becomes available or circumstances change.&#160;&#160;The allowance for loan losses is allocated to loan types using both a formula-based approach applied to groups of loans (general component) and an analysis of certain individual loans for impairment (allocated component).</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">General component</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The general component of the allowance for loan losses covers loans that are collectively evaluated for impairment and is based on historical loss experience adjusted for qualitative factors stratified by loan segments.&#160;&#160; Management uses a rolling average of historical losses based on a trailing <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000437" name="rndb:TimePeriodToCaptureRelevantLoanLossData" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">48</ix:nonNumeric> month time frame appropriate to capture relevant loss data for each loan segment.&#160;&#160;This historical loss factor is supplemented by the following qualitative factors: changes in the volume and severity of past due loans and adversely classified or graded loans, the volume of nonaccrual loans and trends in charge-offs and recoveries&#59; changes in the nature and volume of the portfolio and in the terms of loans&#59; changes in lending policies and procedures, including changes in underwriting standards and collection, charge-off, and recovery practices not considered elsewhere in estimating credit losses&#59; changes in the experience, ability, and depth of lending management and other relevant staff&#59; changes in international, national, regional and local economic and business conditions and developments that affect the collectability of the portfolio, including the condition of various market segments&#59; changes in the quality of the institution&#8217;s review system&#59; the effect of other external factors such as competition and legal and regulatory requirements on the level of estimated credit losses in the institution&#8217;s existing portfolio&#59; changes in the value of underlying collateral-dependent loans&#59; and the existence of concentrations of credit, and changes in the level of such concentrations.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The qualitative factors are determined based on the various risk characteristics of each loan segment.&#160;&#160;Risk characteristics relevant to each portfolio segment are as follows:</p></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-10</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Randolph Bancorp, Inc. and Subsidiary</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (continued)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000342_dcnt_8f2e6828-f0f9-46e1-ae52-f0bd8ed02641" continuedAt="F_000342_dcnt_a8b47f17-e309-412a-b133-2fd3641b5f1f"><ix:continuation id="F_000375_dcnt_e15dbb08-8b25-4d7e-adbd-21609283c08f">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Residential one-to four-family real estate &#8211; The Company generally does not originate loans with a loan-to-value ratio greater than <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000438" name="rndb:LoanToValueRatio" contextRef="C_0001667161_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapAccountsNotesLoansAndFinancingReceivableByReceivableTypeAxis_rndbResidentialOneToFourFamilyRealEstatePortfolioSegmentMember_20201231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">80</ix:nonFraction> percent. All loans in this segment are collateralized by one-to four-family owner, and non-owner-occupied, residential real estate and repayment is dependent on the credit quality of the individual borrower.&#160;&#160;The overall health of the economy, including unemployment rates and housing prices, will have an effect on the credit quality in this segment.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Second mortgages and home equity lines of credit (HELOC) &#8211; Loans in this segment are primarily secured by second-position liens, and the Company may or may not also have a first-position lien.&#160;&#160;Regardless of which creditor is in first position, the Company does not originate loans with a combined loan-to-value ratio greater than <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000439" name="rndb:LoanToValueRatio" contextRef="C_0001667161_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapAccountsNotesLoansAndFinancingReceivableByReceivableTypeAxis_rndbSecondMortgagesAndHomeEquityLinesOfCreditPropertySegmentMember_20201231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">80</ix:nonFraction> percent.&#160;&#160;All loans in this segment are collateralized by owner-occupied residential real estate and repayment is dependent on the credit quality of the individual borrower.&#160;&#160;The overall health of the economy, including unemployment rates and housing prices, will have an effect on the credit quality in this segment.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Commercial real estate &#8211; Loans in this segment consist of owner-occupied and non-owner-occupied property primarily located in Massachusetts and Rhode&#160;Island.&#160;&#160;The underlying cash flows generated by the operating entities of owner-occupied real estate support the associated debt.&#160;&#160;Rental cash flows, for which management obtains periodic rent rolls, support the debt associated with non-owner-occupied real estate and can be negatively impacted by increased vacancy rates.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Construction &#8211; Loans in this segment primarily include residential real estate development loans for which payment is derived from sale of the property.&#160;&#160;Credit risk is affected by cost overruns, time to sell at an adequate price, and market conditions.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Commercial and Industrial &#8211; Loans in this segment are made to businesses and are generally secured by assets of the business.&#160;&#160;Repayment is expected from the cash flows of the business.&#160;&#160;A weakened economy, and resultant decreased consumer spending, would have an effect on the credit quality in this segment. During 2020, the Company funded <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_rndbLoan" id="F_000440" name="rndb:NumberOfPPPLoanFunded" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF">197</ix:nonFraction> PPP loans totaling $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000441" name="rndb:TotalPPPLoanFunded" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">15.4</ix:nonFraction> million. The Company had $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000442" name="rndb:OutstandingPPPLoan" contextRef="C_0001667161_20201231" decimals="-5" scale="6">10.9</ix:nonFraction> million of Paycheck Protection Program (&#8220;PPP&#8221;) loans outstanding at December 31, 2020. These loans are fully guaranteed by the SBA and the Company does not reserve for these loans.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Consumer &#8211; Loans in this segment primarily include personal unsecured loans, refinanced student loans and auto loans purchased from third party lenders. Repayment is dependent on the credit quality of the individual borrower.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Allocated component</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The allocated component of the allowance for loan losses relates to loans that are individually classified as impaired.&#160;&#160;Residential real estate, commercial and industrial, commercial real estate and construction loans are evaluated for impairment on a loan-by-loan basis.&#160;&#160;Impairment is measured by either the present value of expected future cash flows discounted at the loan&#8217;s effective interest rate, or the fair value of the collateral if the loan is collateral dependent.&#160;&#160;An allowance is established when the discounted cash flows (or collateral value) of the impaired loan are lower than the carrying value of that loan.&#160;&#160;Large groups of smaller balance homogeneous loans are collectively evaluated for impairment.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, the Company does not generally identify individual consumer loans or second mortgages and HELOCs for impairment disclosures unless such loans are 90 days past due or are classified as a troubled debt restructuring.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">A loan is considered impaired when, based on current information and events, it is probable that the Company will be unable to collect the scheduled payments of principal or interest when due according to the contractual terms of the loan agreement.&#160;&#160;Factors considered by management in determining impairment include payment status, collateral value, and the probability of collecting scheduled principal and interest payments when due.&#160;&#160;Loans that experience insignificant payment delays and payment shortfalls generally are not classified as impaired.&#160;&#160;Management determines the significance of payment delays and payment shortfalls on a case-by-case basis, taking into consideration all of the circumstances surrounding the loan and the borrower, including the length of the delay, the reasons for the delay, the borrower&#8217;s prior payment record, and the amount of the shortfall in relation to the principal and interest owed.</p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000376" name="rndb:BankOwnedLifeInsurancePolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000376_dcnt_ecdcf801-e405-4314-bae9-9792c3c98cd7">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Bank-owned life insurance</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Bank-owned life insurance policies are reflected on the consolidated balance sheets at their cash surrender value net of charges or other amounts that are probable at settlement.&#160;&#160;Changes in the net cash surrender value of the policies, as well as insurance proceeds received, are reflected in non-interest income in the consolidated statements of operations and are not subject to income taxes, unless such policies are surrendered prior to the death of the insured individuals.</p></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-11</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Randolph Bancorp, Inc. and Subsidiary</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (continued)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000342_dcnt_a8b47f17-e309-412a-b133-2fd3641b5f1f" continuedAt="F_000342_dcnt_b7332f83-4ea1-45f8-b16b-e0c859127313"><ix:continuation id="F_000376_dcnt_ecdcf801-e405-4314-bae9-9792c3c98cd7">
</ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000377" name="us-gaap:LoansAndLeasesReceivableMortgageBankingActivitiesPolicy" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Mortgage servicing rights</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company services mortgage loans for others.&#160;&#160;Mortgage servicing rights are recognized as separate assets at fair value when rights are acquired through purchase or through sale of financial assets (&#8220;MSRs&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Capitalized servicing rights are amortized into mortgage servicing income in proportion to, and over the period of, the estimated future net servicing income of the underlying financial assets.&#160;&#160;MSRs are evaluated for impairment based upon the fair value of the rights as compared to amortized cost.&#160;&#160;Impairment is determined by stratifying rights by predominant risk characteristics, such as interest rates and terms.&#160;&#160;Fair value is based on a valuation model that calculates the present value of estimated future net servicing income, using market-based assumptions.&#160;&#160;Impairment is recognized through a valuation allowance for an individual stratum, to the extent that fair value is less than the capitalized amount for the stratum.&#160;&#160;Changes in the valuation allowance, if any, are reported in mortgage servicing income.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000378" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Premises and equipment</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Land is carried at cost.&#160;&#160;Buildings, equipment and leasehold improvements are stated at cost, less accumulated depreciation and amortization computed predominantly on the straight-line method over the estimated useful lives of the assets or the expected terms of the leases, if shorter.&#160;&#160;Expected terms include lease option periods to the extent that the exercise of such options is reasonably assured.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Premises and equipment held for sale are stated at the lower of amortized cost or fair value less costs to sell.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000379" name="us-gaap:TransfersAndServicingOfFinancialAssetsPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Transfers of financial assets</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Transfers of financial assets are accounted for as sales when control over the assets has been surrendered.&#160;&#160;Control over transferred assets is deemed to be surrendered when (1) the assets have been isolated from the Company, (2) the transferee obtains the right to pledge or exchange the transferred assets, and (3) the Company does not maintain effective control over the transferred assets through an agreement to repurchase them before their maturity.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the normal course of business, the Company may transfer a portion of a financial asset, for example, a participation loan.&#160;&#160;In order to be eligible for sales treatment, all cash flows from the loan must be divided proportionately, the rights of each loan holder must have the same priority, the loan holders must have no recourse to the transferor other than standard representations and warranties, and no loan holder can have the right to pledge or exchange the entire loan.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In certain cases, the Company may have an obligation to repurchase mortgage loans sold to third parties and to refund fees to the purchaser if a payment default or prepayment occurs, in each case within a prescribed time period not exceeding <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000444" name="rndb:ObligationToRepurchaseMortgageLoansPrescribedTimePeriod" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">four months</ix:nonNumeric> after the sale date, or in the case of a violation of its representations and warranties under the provisions of its loan sale agreements. The Company evaluates its obligations under these provisions and recognizes a liability for the fair value of its recourse obligations. At December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019, the Company determined that its obligations in connection with the recourse provisions of its loan sale agreements were insignificant.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000380" name="rndb:ForeclosedRealEstatePolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Foreclosed real estate</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Real estate acquired through, or in lieu of, loan foreclosure are held for sale and are initially recorded at fair value, less costs to sell, at the date of foreclosure, establishing a new cost basis. Subsequent to foreclosure, valuations are periodically performed by management and the assets are carried at the lower of carrying amount or fair value less costs to sell.&#160;&#160;Revenue and expenses from operations, changes in the valuation allowance and any direct write-downs are included in foreclosed real estate expense.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000381" name="us-gaap:PensionAndOtherPostretirementPlansPensionsPolicy" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000381_dcnt_eb9cb702-4adb-41f3-9bc3-d5c434036356">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Supplemental retirement plan</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company accounts for its supplemental retirement plan using an actuarial model that allocates cost over the service period of participants in the plan.&#160;&#160;The Company accounts for the over-funded or under-funded status of the plan as an asset or liability in its consolidated balance sheets and recognizes changes in the funded status in the year in which the changes occur through other comprehensive income/loss.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-12</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Randolph Bancorp, Inc. and Subsidiary</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (continued)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000342_dcnt_b7332f83-4ea1-45f8-b16b-e0c859127313" continuedAt="F_000342_dcnt_8a9df981-4091-4512-b9b7-72069555dde3"><ix:continuation id="F_000381_dcnt_eb9cb702-4adb-41f3-9bc3-d5c434036356">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000382" name="us-gaap:EmployeeStockOwnershipPlanESOPPolicy" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:8pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Employee Stock Ownership Plan </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Compensation expense for the Employee Stock Ownership Plan (&#8220;ESOP&#8221;) is computed based on the number of shares allocated to participants during the period multiplied by the average fair market value of the Company&#8217;s shares.&#160;&#160;This expense is recognized ratably throughout the year based on the expected allocation of shares for the year.&#160;&#160;Unearned compensation applicable to the ESOP is reflected as a reduction of stockholders&#8217; equity. The difference between the average fair market value and cost of the shares allocated by the ESOP is recorded as an adjustment to additional paid-in capital.</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.17%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000383" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationOptionAndIncentivePlansPolicy" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.17%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Stock-based compensation</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.13%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The fair value of restricted stock and stock options is determined on the date of grant and amortized to compensation expense with a corresponding increase to additional paid-in capital over the required service period, but in no event beyond the date of an employee&#8217;s or director&#8217;s date of termination. Forfeitures of unvested awards and grants are recorded as incurred.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000384" name="us-gaap:AdvertisingCostsPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Advertising costs</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Advertising costs are expensed as incurred.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000385" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Income taxes</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Deferred income tax assets and liabilities are determined using the liability (or balance sheet) method.&#160;&#160;Under this method, the net deferred tax asset or liability is determined based on the tax effects of the temporary differences between the book and tax basis of the various balance sheet assets and liabilities and gives current recognition to changes in tax rates and laws.&#160;&#160;A valuation allowance is established against deferred tax assets when, based upon available evidence including historical and projected taxable income, that some or all of the deferred tax assets will not be realized.</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000445" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExaminationLikelihoodOfUnfavorableSettlement" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231"><p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">A tax position is recognized as a benefit if it is &#8220;more likely than not&#8221; that the tax position would be sustained in a tax examination, with a tax examination being presumed to occur. The amount recognized is the largest amount of tax benefit greater than <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000446" name="rndb:PercentageOfTaxBenefitLikelyToBeRealizedOnExamination" contextRef="C_0001667161_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" scale="-2">50</ix:nonFraction>% likely of being realized on examination. For tax positions not meeting the &#8220;more likely than not&#8221; test, no tax benefit is recorded.</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company does not have any uncertain tax positions at December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019 which require accrual or disclosure.&#160;&#160;The Company records interest and penalties as part of income tax expense.&#160;&#160;<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000449" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExaminationPenaltiesAndInterestExpense" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000450" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExaminationPenaltiesAndInterestExpense" contextRef="C_0001667161_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">No</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> interest or penalties were recorded for the years ended December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000386" name="us-gaap:ComprehensiveIncomePolicyPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000386_dcnt_869e16f8-c781-43e1-9287-6bf7461150cf">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Comprehensive income (loss)</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Accounting principles generally require that recognized revenue, expenses, gains and losses be included in net income (loss).&#160;&#160;Although certain changes in assets and liabilities are reported as a separate component of equity, such items, along with net income (loss), are components of comprehensive income (loss).</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000391" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfComprehensiveIncomeLossTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000391_dcnt_26e159e3-afd4-4666-a5e9-515aacefb23a"></ix:nonNumeric></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-13</p>
