<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In 2021, the Company expects to recognize $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000469" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanExpectedAmortizationOfPriorServiceCostCreditNextFiscalYear" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapRetirementPlanTypeAxis_us-gaapSupplementalEmployeeRetirementPlanDefinedBenefitMember_20201231" decimals="0" sign="-" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">45,000</ix:nonFraction> in prior service credits and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000470" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlanExpectedAmortizationOfGainLossNextFiscalYear" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapRetirementPlanTypeAxis_us-gaapSupplementalEmployeeRetirementPlanDefinedBenefitMember_20201231" decimals="0" sign="-" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">62,000</ix:nonFraction> in net actuarial losses as components of cost for the supplemental retirement plan.&#160;&#160;These amounts are included in accumulated other comprehensive loss at December&#160;31, 2020.&#160;&#160;Prior service credits and net actuarial gains and losses are amortized to periodic pension cost over varying periods based on the plan participants to whom they relate.</p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000387" name="us-gaap:SegmentReportingPolicyPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Segment reporting</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:6pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.17%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">An operating segment is defined as a component of a business for which separate financial information is available that is evaluated regularly by the chief operating decision-maker in determining how to allocate resources and evaluate performance. The Company has<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_rndbSegment" id="F_000471" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportableSegments" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen"> two</ix:nonFraction> reporting business segments, namely, &#8220;Envision Bank&#8221; and &#8220;Envision Mortgage&#8221;. Management allocates indirect costs, such as IT, Marketing, Accounting and Administration, to each business segment in order to fully measure each segment&#8217;s results of operations. See Note 18 for disclosure of the Company&#8217;s segment information.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000388" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerSharePolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:8pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Earnings per share</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-size:6pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Basic earnings per share represents income available to common stockholders divided by the weighted average of common shares outstanding during the period. Unvested restricted shares of common stock having dividend rights are treated as &#8220;participating securities&#8221; and, accordingly, are considered outstanding in computing basic earnings per share. Unallocated ESOP shares are not considered outstanding in computing earnings per share. Diluted earnings per share reflects additional common shares that would have been outstanding if dilutive potential shares had been issued. Stock options represent potential dilutive shares with the number of such shares computed using the treasury stock method. &#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000389" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationsPolicy" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:8pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Business combinations</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:6pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We account for business combinations under the acquisition method of accounting. The application of this method of accounting requires the use of significant estimates and assumptions in the determination of the fair value of tangible and identified intangible assets acquired and liabilities assumed in order to properly allocate purchase price consideration between assets from those that are recorded as goodwill. Our estimates of the fair values of assets acquired and liabilities assumed are based upon assumptions that we believe to be reasonable, and whenever necessary, include assistance from independent third-party appraisal and valuation firms. Costs incurred to consummate a business combination are expensed as incurred.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000390" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000390_dcnt_cd38c28e-5cb7-464f-8cc7-dfe7f6105554">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:8pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Recent accounting pronouncements</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:6pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:5%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On January 1, 2019, the Company early adopted Accounting Standards Update (&#8220;ASU&#8221;) No. 2014-09, <span style="font-style:italic;">Revenue from Contracts with Customers. </span>This Update provides a revenue recognition framework for any entity that either enters into contracts with customers to<span style="font-style:italic;"> </span>transfer goods or services or enters into contracts for the transfer of non-financial assets unless those contracts are within the scope of<span style="font-style:italic;"> </span>other accounting standards. The Company&#8217;s revenues relate principally to financial instruments, which are explicitly excluded from<span style="font-style:italic;"> </span>the scope of this Update. The impact to the consolidated financial statements upon adopting ASU 2014-09 was not material. See Note<span style="font-style:italic;"> </span>16 for additional information.</p></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-14</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Randolph Bancorp, Inc. and Subsidiary</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (continued)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000342_dcnt_77d1b293-925b-483c-ba29-24d930f0fcdb" continuedAt="F_000342_dcnt_78c2abd4-9544-4d75-94c3-5defb2f08c1c"><ix:continuation id="F_000390_dcnt_cd38c28e-5cb7-464f-8cc7-dfe7f6105554" continuedAt="F_000390_dcnt_b651eb5f-b2c7-4b3c-bd55-ed689bb409b0">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:5%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:5%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In January 2016, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;) issued ASU 2016-01, <span style="font-style:italic;">Financial Instruments</span>. This ASU revises the accounting related to the classification and measurement of investments in equity securities, and the presentation of certain fair value changes for financial liabilities measured at fair value. It also amends certain disclosure requirements associated with the fair value of financial instruments to require use of an exit pricing notion. This ASU is effective for emerging growth companies for annual periods beginning after December 31, 2018, and interim periods beginning after December 31, 2019. The Company adopted this ASU effective December 31, 2019. The impact of adoption of this ASU is limited to disclosure of the fair value of financial instruments.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:5%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:5%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In February 2016, FASB issued ASU 2016-02, <span style="font-style:italic;">Leases</span>. This ASU requires lessees to put most leases on their balance sheets but recognize expenses on their income statements in a manner similar to current accounting requirements. In May 2020, FASB amended the effective date of the new guidance on leases. Previously, the amendments and related new guidance on leases were effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2020, and interim periods within fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2021 and interim periods within fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2022. Early adoption is still permitted. Due to the Company&#8217;s Emerging Growth Company status expiring on December 31, 2021, this pronouncement will be effective for the fiscal period ending December 31, 2021 and for interim reporting periods thereafter. The Company&#8217;s assets and liabilities will increase based on the present value of remaining lease payments for leases in place at the time of adoption. The Company is currently assessing the impact of the adoption of this ASU on its consolidated balance sheet.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:5%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:5%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In June 2016, the FASB issued ASU 2016-13, <span style="font-style:italic;">Financial Instruments &#8211; Credit Losses</span>. The ASU sets forth a &#8220;current expected credit loss&#8221; (&#8220;CECL&#8221;) model which requires the Company to measure all expected credit losses for financial instruments held at the reporting date based on historical experience, current conditions and reasonable and supportable forecasts. This replaces the existing probable incurred loss model and is applicable to the measurement of credit losses on financial assets measured at amortized cost and applies to some off-balance sheet credit exposures. This ASU requires enhanced disclosures to help investors and other financial statement users better understand significant estimates and judgements used in determining the allowance for loan losses, as well as the credit quality and underwriting standards of an organization&#8217;s loan portfolio. In addition, the ASU amends the accounting for credit losses on available for sale debt securities and purchased financial assets with credit deterioration. In November 2019, FASB issued ASU 2019-10 which extended the effective date for adoption of ASU 2016-13 for smaller reporting companies to fiscal years beginning after December 31, 2022, including interim periods therein. Early adoption is permitted. The Company has formed a working group consisting of accounting, credit and data systems personnel to lead our implementation of this ASU. The working group is evaluating the alternative methodologies which are available and has engaged professional advisors to assist in implementation.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:5%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:5%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In April 2017, the FASB issued ASU 2017-08 <span style="font-style:italic;">Receivables &#8211; Non-refundable Fees and Other Costs</span>, which shortens the period of amortization of the premium on certain callable debt securities to the earliest call date. Currently, GAAP excludes certain callable debt securities from consideration of early repayment of principal even if the holder is certain that the call will be exercised. As a result, upon the exercise of a call on a callable debt security held at a premium, the unamortized premium is recorded as a loss in earnings. This ASU requires that premiums on certain callable debt securities be amortized to the shortest call date. Securities within the scope of this paragraph are those that have explicit, noncontingent call features that are callable at fixed prices and on preset dates. This ASU is effective for emerging growth companies for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2019, including interim periods therein. The impact of adopting this ASU is dependent on the materiality of callable debt securities meeting the specific criteria set forth therein at the time of adoption. The Company adopted the standard January 1, 2020.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:5.06%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In August 2018, the FASB issued ASU 2018-13 <span style="font-style:italic;">Fair Value Measurement &#8211; Changes to the Disclosure Requirements for Fair Value Measurement, </span>which removes the disclosure requirements for transfers between Levels 1 and 2 of the fair value hierarchy, the policy for timing of transfers between levels of the fair value hierarchy and the valuation processes for Level 3 fair value measurements. This ASU also adds disclosure requirements for the changes in unrealized gains and losses included in other comprehensive income for recurring Level 3 fair value measurements and the range and weighted average of significant unobservable inputs used to develop Level 3 measurements. This ASU is effective for emerging growth companies for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2019, including interim periods therein. The Company adopted the standard January 1, 2020.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:5%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:5%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In December 2019, FASB issued ASU 2019-12, <span style="font-style:italic;">Income Taxes &#8211; Simplifying the Accounting for Income Taxes</span>. This ASU removes certain exceptions for recognizing deferred taxes for investments, performing intraperiod allocation and calculating income taxes in interim periods. The ASU also adds guidance to reduce complexity in certain areas, including eliminating the exception to the requirement that the tax effect of income from continuing operations should be determined without considering </p></ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-15</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Randolph Bancorp, Inc. and Subsidiary</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (continued)</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:5%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">the tax effect of items that are not included in continuing operations such as items included in other comprehensive income (loss).</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> This ASU is effective for emerging growth companies for annual periods beginning after December </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">15</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">, 20</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">21</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">, and interim periods beginning after December </span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">15</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">, 20</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">22</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">. The impact of adoption of this ASU is limited</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> and not expected to be material</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">.</span></p></ix:continuation>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Management performs a discounted cash flow calculation to determine the amount of impairment reserve required on each of the troubled debt restructurings.&#160;&#160;Any reserve required is recorded as part of the allowance for loan losses.&#160;&#160;At December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019 allowances of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000811" name="rndb:AllowanceForCreditLossesChangeInMethodOfCalculatingTroubledDebtRestructuring" contextRef="C_0001667161_20201231" decimals="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">133,000</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000812" name="rndb:AllowanceForCreditLossesChangeInMethodOfCalculatingTroubledDebtRestructuring" contextRef="C_0001667161_20191231" decimals="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">116,000</ix:nonFraction>, respectively, related to troubled debt restructurings.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During the years ended December 31, 2020 and 2019, there were <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000813" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableModificationsSubsequentDefaultRecordedInvestment1" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapFinancingReceivablesPeriodPastDueAxis_us-gaapFinancingReceivables30To59DaysPastDueMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000814" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableModificationsSubsequentDefaultRecordedInvestment1" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapFinancingReceivablesPeriodPastDueAxis_us-gaapFinancingReceivables30To59DaysPastDueMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">no</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> troubled debt restructurings that defaulted (over 30 days past due) within twelve months of the restructure date. <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000815" name="us-gaap:LoansAndLeasesReceivableImpairedCommitmentToLend" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapFinancingReceivablesPeriodPastDueAxis_us-gaapFinancingReceivables30To59DaysPastDueMember_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">No</ix:nonFraction> additional funds are committed to be advanced on loans being accounted for as troubled debt restructurings.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At December 31, 2020, there were <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_rndbTDR" id="F_000816" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableModificationsSubsequentDefaultNumberOfContracts1" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapFinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis_us-gaapResidentialPortfolioSegmentMember_us-gaapLoanRestructuringModificationAxis_us-gaapPaymentDeferralMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">two</ix:nonFraction> residential real estate troubled debt restructurings that were granted payment deferral plans. One loan, totaling $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000817" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableModificationsRecordedInvestment" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapFinancialInstrumentPerformanceStatusAxis_us-gaapPerformingFinancingReceivableMember_us-gaapFinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis_us-gaapResidentialPortfolioSegmentMember_us-gaapLoanRestructuringModificationAxis_us-gaapPaymentDeferralMember_20201231" decimals="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">298,000</ix:nonFraction>, was performing in accordance with its modified terms and is currently in repayment, and one loan, for $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000818" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableModificationsRecordedInvestment" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapFinancialInstrumentPerformanceStatusAxis_us-gaapNonperformingFinancingReceivableMember_us-gaapFinancingReceivablePortfolioSegmentAxis_us-gaapResidentialPortfolioSegmentMember_us-gaapLoanRestructuringModificationAxis_us-gaapPaymentDeferralMember_20201231" decimals="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">196,000</ix:nonFraction> was not performing in accordance with its modified terms and is currently still in payment suspense.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Credit Quality Information</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company utilizes an eight-grade internal loan rating system for commercial real estate, construction and commercial loans, as follows:</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:9.06%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Loans rated 1 &#8211; 3A are considered &#8220;pass&#8221; rated loans with low to average risk.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:9.06%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Loans rated 4 are considered &#8220;special mention.&#8221;&#160;&#160;These loans are starting to show signs of potential weakness and are being closely monitored by management.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:9.06%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Loans rated 5 are considered &#8220;substandard&#8221; and are inadequately protected by the current net worth and paying capacity of the obligors and/or the collateral pledged.&#160;&#160;There is a distinct possibility that the Company will sustain some loss if the weakness is not corrected.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:9.06%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Loans rated 6 are considered &#8220;doubtful&#8221; and have all the weaknesses inherent in those classified substandard with the added characteristic that the weaknesses make collection or liquidation in full, on the basis of currently existing facts, highly questionable and improbable.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:9.06%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Loans rated 7 are considered uncollectible (&#8220;loss&#8221;) and of such little value that their continuance as loans is not warranted.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On an annual basis, or more often if needed, the Company formally reviews the ratings on all commercial real estate, construction and commercial loans.&#160;&#160;Annually, the Company engages an independent third party to review a significant portion of loans within these segments.&#160;&#160;Management uses the results of these reviews as part of its annual review process.</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000400" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableCreditQualityIndicatorsTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000400_dcnt_c5714ecf-82c6-4edf-9c58-d2ae00b0d439"></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Total depreciation and amortization expense for the years ended December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019 amounted to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000897" name="us-gaap:DepreciationAndAmortization" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" decimals="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">1,508,000</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000898" name="us-gaap:DepreciationAndAmortization" contextRef="C_0001667161_20190101_20191231" decimals="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">857,000</ix:nonFraction>, respectively.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.17%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During 2017, the Company amended the lease for its Andover loan operations center relocating offices within an office complex. As part of this lease amendment, the landlord funded the cost of leasehold improvements which amounted to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000899" name="rndb:LeaseholdImprovementsFundedByLandlord" contextRef="C_0001667161_20170101_20171231" decimals="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">646,000</ix:nonFraction>. These costs have been capitalized as part of premises and equipment and a tenant improvement allowance has been recorded as part of other liabilities in the accompanying consolidated balance sheet. Both the leasehold improvements and tenant improvement allowance are being amortized over the initial lease term of approximately <ix:nonNumeric id="F_000900" name="rndb:LeaseholdImprovementsAllowanceAmortizationPeriod" contextRef="C_0001667161_20170101_20171231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000901" name="rndb:TenantImprovementAllowanceAmortizationPeriod" contextRef="C_0001667161_20170101_20171231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">five years</ix:nonNumeric></ix:nonNumeric>.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.17%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.17%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In July 2018, the Company entered into a sublease agreement for <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_000902" name="rndb:PercentageOfLandOccupiedUnderSubleaseAgreement" contextRef="C_0001667161_20180731_20180731" decimals="2" scale="-2">27</ix:nonFraction>% of the space in its Andover location. This sublease commenced on October 1, 2018 and runs co-terminus with the Company&#8217;s lease which expires in <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:F_000903">March 2023</span>. &#160; </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.17%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.17%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In October 2018, the Board of Directors approved a plan to consolidate mortgage banking operations in the Company&#8217;s North Attleboro loan operations center (see Note 20 for additional information). As part of this decision, certain mortgage banking employees not directly involved in the loan origination process remained at the Andover location. Based on an analysis of space needs for the remaining employees, the area not currently under sublease was subdivided resulting in approximately half of the total leased space in Andover becoming available for sublease. In connection with these actions, the Company recognized a fair value &#8220;cease use&#8221; liability of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000904" name="rndb:FairValueCeaseUseLiability" contextRef="C_0001667161_srtStatementGeographicalAxis_rndbAndoverMember_us-gaapRestructuringPlanAxis_rndbConsolidationOfMortgageBankingOperationsMember_20181231" decimals="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">565,000</ix:nonFraction> based on estimated future cash flows which is included in the restructuring charge recorded in the fourth quarter of 2018. This space remained unoccupied and the Company adjusted the cease use liability at December 31, 2019 on the assumption that this space will continue to be unoccupied through the lease term which ends in March 2023. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.17%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.17%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In December of 2020, the Board of Directors approved a plan to consolidated mortgage banking operations to its Salem, New Hampshire location. As part of this decision, all mortgage banking employees located in the Andover, Massachusetts location were relocated to Salem or will work remotely. In connection with these actions, the Company recognized a fair value &#8220;cease use&#8221; liability of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_000905" name="rndb:FairValueCeaseUseLiability" contextRef="C_0001667161_srtStatementGeographicalAxis_rndbSalemNewHampshireMember_us-gaapRestructuringPlanAxis_rndbConsolidationOfMortgageBankingOperationsMember_20201231" decimals="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">294,000</ix:nonFraction> based on estimated future cash flows for the Andover lease and sublease agreements. The space allocated to the Company remains unoccupied and the Company adjusted the cease use liability on the assumption that this space will continue to be unoccupied through the lease term which ends in March 2023. The Company will continue to collect income on its sublease agreement until that agreement expires in March 2023.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.17%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>

<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (continued)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000349_dcnt_c87287bc-2edb-4f79-9884-ddd4b191a5c9">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">From 2014 to June 30, 2020, the Company has maintained a valuation allowance on its net deferred tax asset based on a determination that it was more likely than not that such assets would not be realized. This determination was based on the Company's net operating loss carryforward position, its current period operating results exclusive of non-recurring items and its expectations for the upcoming year. As a result, the <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001071" name="rndb:DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowancePercentage" contextRef="C_0001667161_20201231" decimals="2" scale="-2">100</ix:nonFraction>% valuation allowance for deferred tax assets relating to the net operating loss carryforwards was maintained. Due to the level of income earned during the year ended 2020 and the Company being in a net deferred tax liability position at December 31, 2020, the full amount of the Company&#8217;s net operating loss carryforwards was absorbed and the previously held valuation allowance was reversed. &#160;The Company continues to maintain a valuation allowance for its charitable contribution carryforward as management concluded that improvements to operating earnings, while significant, would need to be sustained for an additional period to provide sufficient evidence that realizability of the deferred tax asset was more likely than not to occur.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">At December 31, 2020, the Company has a charitable contribution carryforward of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001072" name="rndb:CharitableContributionCarryforwards" contextRef="C_0001667161_20201231" decimals="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">531,000</ix:nonFraction> of which all but $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001073" name="rndb:CharitableContributionCarryforwards" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapTaxCreditCarryforwardAxis_rndbDeferredTaxAssetsCharitableContributionCarryforwardExpirationDateMember_20201231" decimals="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">77,000</ix:nonFraction> expires on &#160;<ix:nonNumeric id="F_001074" name="rndb:DeferredTaxAssetsCharitableContributionCarryforwardExpirationDate" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapTaxCreditCarryforwardAxis_rndbDeferredTaxAssetsCharitableContributionCarryforwardExpirationDateMember_20200101_20201231" format="ixt:datemonthdayyearen">December 31, 2021</ix:nonNumeric>.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.17%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160; &#160;</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:bold;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">ON-BALANCE SHEET DERIVATIVE INSTRUMENTS AND HEDGING ACTIVITIES</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Derivative Loan Commitments</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Mortgage loan interest rate lock commitments qualify as derivative loan commitments if the loan that will result from exercise of the commitment will be held for sale upon funding.&#160;&#160;The Company enters into commitments to fund residential mortgage loans at specified rates and times in the future, with the intention that these loans will subsequently be sold in the secondary market or to other financial institutions.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Outstanding derivative loan commitments expose the Company to the risk that the price of the loans arising from exercise of the loan commitment might decline from inception of the rate lock to funding of the loan due to an increase in mortgage interest rates.&#160;&#160;If interest rates increase, the value of these loan commitments decreases.&#160;&#160;Conversely, if interest rates decrease, the value of these loan commitments increases.&#160;&#160;The notional amount of derivative loan commitments was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001078" name="us-gaap:DerivativeNotionalAmount" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapFinancialInstrumentAxis_rndbDerivativeLoanCommitmentsMember_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">396,551,000</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001079" name="us-gaap:DerivativeNotionalAmount" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapFinancialInstrumentAxis_rndbDerivativeLoanCommitmentsMember_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">89,925,000</ix:nonFraction> at December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019, respectively.&#160;&#160;The fair value of such commitments at December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019 was an asset of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001080" name="us-gaap:DerivativeAssets" <p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Forward Loan Sale Commitments</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company utilizes both &#8220;mandatory delivery&#8221; and &#8220;best efforts&#8221; forward loan sale commitments and, effective in the fourth quarter of 2018, TBA securities to hedge the financial impact of changes in interest rates on the value of loans that would result from the exercise of the derivative loan commitments.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">With a &#8220;mandatory delivery&#8221; contract, the Company commits to deliver a certain principal amount of mortgage loans to an investor at a specified price on or before a specified date.&#160;&#160;If the Company fails to deliver the amount of mortgages necessary to fulfill the commitment by the specified date, it may be obligated to pay a &#8220;pair-off&#8221; fee, based on then-current market prices, to the investor to compensate the investor in the event of a loss in value.</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-27</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Randolph Bancorp, Inc. and Subsidiary</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (continued)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000350_dcnt_f2a6d010-15c6-4648-837c-84d73f3fedf9">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">With a &#8220;best efforts&#8221; contract, the Company commits to deliver an individual mortgage loan of a specified principal amount and quality to an investor if the loan to the underlying borrower closes.&#160;&#160;Generally, the price the investor will pay the seller for an individual loan is specified prior to the loan being funded (e.g., on the same day the lender commits to lend funds to a potential borrower).</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company expects that these forward loan sale commitments and TBA securities will experience changes in fair value that serve to substantially offset the change in fair value of derivative loan commitments the degree to which depends on the notional amount of such sale commitments.&#160;&#160;The aggregate notional amount of forward loan sale commitments and TBA securities was $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001084" name="us-gaap:DerivativeNotionalAmount" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapFinancialInstrumentAxis_rndbForwardLoanSaleCommitmentsAndToBeAnnouncedSecuritiesMember_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">390,248,000</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001085" name="us-gaap:DerivativeNotionalAmount" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapFinancialInstrumentAxis_rndbForwardLoanSaleCommitmentsAndToBeAnnouncedSecuritiesMember_20191231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">85,401,000</ix:nonFraction> at December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019, respectively. The fair value of such commitments at December 31, 2020 and 2019 consisted of liabilities of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001086" name="us-gaap:DerivativeLiabilities" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapBalanceSheetLocationAxis_us-gaapOtherLiabilitiesMember_us-gaapFinancialInstrumentAxis_rndbForwardLoanSaleCommitmentsAndToBeAnnouncedSecuritiesMember_20201231" decimals="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">2,180,000</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001087" name="us-gaap:DerivativeLiabilities" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapBalanceSheetLocationAxis_us-gaapOtherLiabilitiesMember_us-gaapFinancialInstrumentAxis_rndbForwardLoanSaleCommitmentsAndToBeAnnouncedSecuritiesMember_20191231" decimals="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">140,000</ix:nonFraction>, respectively, included in other liabilities in the consolidated balance sheets and assets of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001088" name="us-gaap:DerivativeAssets" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapBalanceSheetLocationAxis_us-gaapOtherAssetsMember_us-gaapFinancialInstrumentAxis_rndbForwardLoanSaleCommitmentsAndToBeAnnouncedSecuritiesMember_20201231" decimals="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">44,000</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001089" name="us-gaap:DerivativeAssets" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapBalanceSheetLocationAxis_us-gaapOtherAssetsMember_us-gaapFinancialInstrumentAxis_rndbForwardLoanSaleCommitmentsAndToBeAnnouncedSecuritiesMember_20191231" decimals="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">11,000</ix:nonFraction>, respectively, included in other assets in the consolidated balance sheets. During the years ended December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019, net increases (reductions) in the aggregate fair value liability of $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001090" name="us-gaap:DerivativeGainLossOnDerivativeNet" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapFinancialInstrumentAxis_rndbForwardLoanSaleCommitmentsAndToBeAnnouncedSecuritiesMember_us-gaapIncomeStatementLocationAxis_rndbNetGainOnSalesOfMortgageLoansMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">2,007,000</ix:nonFraction> and ($<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001091" name="us-gaap:DerivativeGainLossOnDerivativeNet" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapFinancialInstrumentAxis_rndbForwardLoanSaleCommitmentsAndToBeAnnouncedSecuritiesMember_us-gaapIncomeStatementLocationAxis_rndbNetGainOnSalesOfMortgageLoansMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="0" sign="-" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">124,000</ix:nonFraction>), respectively, related to forward loan sale commitments and TBA securities were recognized and included in net gain on loan originations and sales activities in the accompanying consolidated statements of operations.</p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000351" name="us-gaap:RegulatoryCapitalRequirementsUnderBankingRegulationsTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000351_dcnt_cc410eaf-43f3-4eb8-8fe1-845219258b73">

<td valign="top">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:bold;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">MINIMUM REGULATORY CAPITAL REQUIREMENTS</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Bank is subject to various regulatory capital requirements administered by federal banking agencies.&#160;&#160;Capital adequacy guidelines and prompt corrective actions regulations involve qualitative measures of assets, liabilities, and certain off-balance sheet items calculated under regulatory accounting practices.&#160;&#160;Capital amounts and classifications are also subject to qualitative judgement by regulators.&#160;&#160;Failure to meet capital requirements can initiate regulatory action.&#160;&#160;The final rules implementing Basel Committee on Banking Supervision&#8217;s capital guidelines for U.S. banks (Basel III rules) became effective for the Bank on January 1, 2015. Under BASEL III, community banking institutions must maintain a capital conservation buffer of common equity tier 1 capital in an amount greater than <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001092" name="us-gaap:ExcessCapitalToRiskWeightedAssets" contextRef="C_0001667161_srtRangeAxis_srtMinimumMember_20201231" decimals="3" scale="-2">2.5</ix:nonFraction>% of total risk-weighted assets to avoid being subject to limitations on capital distributions and discretionary bonuses. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Quantitative measures established by regulation to ensure capital adequacy require the Bank to maintain minimum amounts and ratios (set forth in the following tables) of total, Tier&#160;1 capital and common equity Tier 1 capital to risk weighted assets, and Tier&#160;1 capital to average assets (all as defined). Management believes, as of December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019, that the Bank met all capital adequacy requirements to which it is subject.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of December&#160;31, 2020, the most recent notification from the FDIC categorized the Bank as well capitalized under the regulatory framework for prompt corrective action.&#160;&#160;To be categorized as well capitalized, the Bank must maintain minimum total risk-based, Tier&#160;1 risk-based, common equity Tier 1 and Tier&#160;1 leverage ratios as set forth in the following tables.&#160;&#160;There are no conditions or events since the notification that management believes have changed the Bank&#8217;s category.</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000411" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfComplianceWithRegulatoryCapitalRequirementsUnderBankingRegulationsTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000411_cnt_1">

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Endorsement split-dollar life insurance arrangements</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">401(k) Plan</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><ix:nonNumeric id="F_001193" name="us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPlansGeneralInformation" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapRetirementPlanTypeAxis_rndbFourZeroOneKPlanMember_20200101_20201231">The Company maintains a 401(k) Plan whereby each employee reaching the age of 21 automatically becomes a participant in the plan.&#160;&#160;Employees may contribute up to <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001195" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanMaximumAnnualContributionsPerEmployeePercent" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapRetirementPlanTypeAxis_rndbFourZeroOneKPlanMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="2" scale="-2">15</ix:nonFraction>% of their compensation subject to certain limits based on federal tax laws. All employees who have worked for <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001196" name="rndb:MinimumNumberOfYearWorkedByEmployees" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapRetirementPlanTypeAxis_rndbFourZeroOneKPlanMember_20200101_20201231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">one year</ix:nonNumeric> or 1,000 hours are eligible for an automatic employer contribution of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001198" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanEmployerMatchingContributionPercent" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapRetirementPlanTypeAxis_rndbFourZeroOneKPlanMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="2" scale="-2">3</ix:nonFraction>% of employees&#8217; compensation, which requires no vesting period.</ix:nonNumeric> The Company also matches <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001200" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanEmployerMatchingContributionPercentOfMatch" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapRetirementPlanTypeAxis_rndbFourZeroOneKPlanMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="2" scale="-2">50</ix:nonFraction>% of the first <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001201" name="rndb:EmployerMatchOfEligibleEmployeesContributionsPercentage" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapRetirementPlanTypeAxis_rndbFourZeroOneKPlanMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="2" scale="-2">2</ix:nonFraction>% of an eligible employee&#8217;s contributions, allowing for a total employer contribution of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001202" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanEmployerMatchingContributionPercent" contextRef="C_0001667161_srtRangeAxis_srtMaximumMember_us-gaapRetirementPlanTypeAxis_rndbFourZeroOneKPlanMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="2" scale="-2">4</ix:nonFraction>% of employees&#8217; compensation.&#160;&#160;Matching contributions vest over a <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001203" name="rndb:EmployerMatchingContributionsVestingPeriod" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapRetirementPlanTypeAxis_rndbFourZeroOneKPlanMember_20200101_20201231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">four year</ix:nonNumeric> service period.&#160;&#160;In addition, a profit-sharing provision allows for an additional discretionary contribution by the Company upon approval of the Board of Directors.&#160;&#160;For the years ended December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019, expense attributable to the 401(k) Plan amounted to $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001204" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanCostRecognized" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapRetirementPlanTypeAxis_rndbFourZeroOneKPlanMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">852,000</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD" id="F_001205" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanCostRecognized" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapRetirementPlanTypeAxis_rndbFourZeroOneKPlanMember_20190101_20191231" decimals="0" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">753,000</ix:nonFraction>, respectively, with no additional discretionary contribution made.</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company maintains an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (&#8220;ESOP&#8221;), which is a tax-qualified retirement plan providing eligible employees the opportunity to own Company stock. The Company granted a loan to the ESOP for the purchase of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlishares" id="F_001274" name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesEmployeeStockOwnershipPlan" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapRelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis_rndbFoundationMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">469,498</ix:nonFraction> shares of its common stock at $<ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_iso4217USD_xbrlishares" id="F_001275" name="us-gaap:SaleOfStockPricePerShare" contextRef="C_0001667161_us-gaapStatementEquityComponentsAxis_us-gaapCommonStockMember_20201231" decimals="INF">10.00</ix:nonFraction> per share. The loan is payable annually over <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001276" name="rndb:TermOfLoanRepaidByEmployeeStockOwnershipPlan" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" format="ixt-sec:duryear">25</ix:nonNumeric> years with interest at the prime rate to be reset each January 1<sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top">st</sup>. The interest rate in effect for the years ended December&#160;31, 2020 and 2019 was <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001277" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateDuringPeriod" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" decimals="4" scale="-2">4.75</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_xbrlipure" id="F_001278" name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateDuringPeriod" contextRef="C_0001667161_20190101_20191231" decimals="4" scale="-2">5.50</ix:nonFraction>%, respectively. The loan is secured by the shares which have not yet been allocated to participants. Loan payments are funded by cash contributions from the Bank. Such contributions are allocated to eligible participants based on their compensation, subject to federal tax limits. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Shares are committed to be released on a monthly basis and allocated as of December 31<sup style="font-size:85%;line-height:120%;vertical-align:top">st</sup> of each year. <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company is a party to financial instruments with off-balance-sheet risk in the normal course of business to meet the financing needs of its customers.&#160;&#160;These financial instruments include commitments to extend credit.&#160;&#160;These instruments involve, to varying degrees, elements of market, credit and interest rate risk which are not recognized in the consolidated financial statements.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s exposure to credit loss is represented by the contractual amount of these commitments.&#160;&#160;The Company uses the same credit policies in making commitments and conditional obligations as it does for on-balance-sheet instruments.</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000421" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfFairValueOffBalanceSheetRisksTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true">

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:2pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Commitments to extend credit are agreements to lend to a customer as long as there is no violation of any condition established in the contract.&#160;&#160;Commitments generally have fixed expiration dates or other termination clauses and may require payment of a fee.&#160;&#160;The commitments for lines of credit may expire without being drawn upon.&#160;&#160;Therefore, the total commitment amounts do not necessarily represent future cash requirements.&#160;&#160;The Company evaluates each customer&#8217;s creditworthiness on a case-by-case basis.&#160;&#160;The majority of these financial instruments are collateralized by real estate.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Employment Arrangement and Change in Control Agreements</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company has entered into an employment arrangement with its President and Chief Executive Officer that provides for <ix:nonNumeric id="F_001330" name="rndb:SalaryContinuationTermOfEmploymentArrangement" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">three years</ix:nonNumeric> of salary continuation in the event his employment is terminated without cause or he resigns for good reason, subject to his providing a release of claims and complying with a non-solicitation and non-disclosure agreement. </p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-34</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Randolph Bancorp, Inc. and Subsidiary</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (continued)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000357_dcnt_82b05264-3264-4fca-ad75-da7f747f34e0">

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company has also entered into change in control agreements with <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_rndbMember" id="F_001331" name="rndb:NumberOfMembersWithChangeInControlAgreements" contextRef="C_0001667161_srtTitleOfIndividualAxis_rndbFiveMembersOfSeniorManagementMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">five</ix:nonFraction> members of senior management which provide that if, within two years of a change of control of the Company or the Bank, the executive is involuntarily terminated other than for cause, disability or death, or voluntarily resigns for good reason, the executive will be entitled to a lump-sum payment equal to two times salary plus bonus. The Company has also entered into change in control agreements with <ix:nonFraction unitRef="U_rndbMember" id="F_001332" name="rndb:NumberOfMembersWithChangeInControlAgreements" contextRef="C_0001667161_srtTitleOfIndividualAxis_rndbFourMembersOfSeniorManagementMember_20200101_20201231" decimals="INF" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">four</ix:nonFraction> members of senior management which provide that if, within one year of a change of control of the Company or the Bank, the executive is involuntarily terminated other than for cause, disability or death, or voluntarily resigns for good reason, the executive will be entitled to a lump-sum payment equal to one times salary plus bonus.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Other contingencies</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company is not currently a party to any pending legal proceedings that it believes would have a material adverse effect on its financial condition, results of operations or cash flows.</p></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000358" name="us-gaap:FairValueDisclosuresTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000358_dcnt_7b3a1b46-23fb-4530-a642-f9391858563f">
<div style="align:left;">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:4.54%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">1</span><span style="font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">7</span><span style="font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">.</span></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:bold;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">FAIR VALUE OF ASSETS AND LIABILITIES</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Determination of fair value</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company uses fair value measurements to record fair value adjustments to certain assets and liabilities and to determine fair value disclosures.&#160;&#160;Fair value is the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date.&#160;&#160;Fair value is best determined based upon quoted market prices.&#160;&#160;However, in many instances, there are no quoted market prices for the Company&#8217;s various assets and liabilities.&#160;&#160;In cases where quoted market prices are not available, fair values are based on estimates using present value or other valuation techniques.&#160;&#160;Those techniques are significantly affected by the assumptions used, including the discount rate and estimates of future cash flows.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, the fair value estimates may not be realized in an immediate settlement of the asset or liability.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The following methods and assumptions were used by the Company in estimating fair value disclosures:</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:9.06%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Cash and cash equivalents</span> &#8211; The carrying amounts of cash and short-term instruments approximate fair values based on the short-term nature of the assets.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:9.06%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Certificates of deposit</span> &#8211; Certificates of deposit are carried at cost. These assets are measured at fair value in level 2 based on pricing models that consider standard input factors such as observable market data, benchmark yields, interest rate volatilities, broker/dealer quotes, credit spreads and new issue data.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:9.06%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Securities</span> &#8211; All fair value measurements are obtained from a third-party pricing service and are not adjusted by management.&#160;&#160;The securities measured at fair value in Level 1 are based on quoted market prices in an active exchange market.&#160;&#160;Securities measured at fair value in Level 2 are based on pricing models that consider standard input factors such as observable market data, benchmark yields, interest rate volatilities, broker/dealer quotes, credit spreads and new issue data.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:9.06%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Federal Home Loan Bank of Boston stock</span> &#8211; It is not practical to determine the fair value of FHLBB stock due to restrictions on its transferability.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:9.06%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Loans held for sale</span> &#8211; Fair values are based on commitments in effect from investors or prevailing market prices.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:9.06%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Loans</span> &#8211; Fair values are based on the exit price notion, which is what would be received to sell the loan in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. The valuation model takes into consideration internal financial reports, charge-off history for the Bank and peers and market interest rate information.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:9.06%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Mortgage servicing rights</span> &#8211; Fair value is based on a valuation model that calculates the present value of estimated future net servicing income, using various assumptions related to fees, discount rates and prepayment speeds.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:9.06%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Deposit liabilities</span> &#8211; The fair values disclosed for demand deposits (e.g., interest and non-interest checking, passbook savings, and money market accounts) are, by definition, equal to the amount payable on demand at the reporting date (i.e., their carrying amounts).&#160;&#160;Fair values for fixed-rate term certificates are estimated using a discounted cash flow calculation that applies market interest rates currently being offered on certificates to a schedule of aggregated expected monthly maturities.</p></ix:nonNumeric>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">F-35</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always" />
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Randolph Bancorp, Inc. and Subsidiary</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (continued)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</p><ix:continuation id="F_000358_dcnt_7b3a1b46-23fb-4530-a642-f9391858563f" continuedAt="F_000358_dcnt_37b02d58-03cd-44d9-8ae4-05188ffb9ca6">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:9.06%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">FHLBB advances</span><span style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> - The fair values of the Company&#8217;s FHLBB advances are estimated using discounted cash flow analyses based on the current borrowing rates in the market for similar types of borrowing arrangements.</span></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:9.06%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Accrued interest</span> - The carrying amounts of accrued interest approximate fair value.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:9.06%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">On-balance-sheet derivatives</span> Fair values of forward loan sale commitments, including TBAs, and derivative loan commitments are based on fair values of the underlying mortgage loans and, for derivative loan commitments, fair values also include the value of servicing, costs to be incurred to close loans and the probability of such commitments being exercised. Significant management judgment and estimation is required in determining these fair value measurements.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:9.06%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><span style="text-decoration:underline;">Off-balance sheet credit-related instruments</span> - Fair values for off-balance-sheet, credit-related financial instruments are based on fees currently charged to enter into similar agreements, taking into account the remaining terms of the agreements and the counterparties&#8217; credit standing.&#160;&#160;The fair values of these instruments are not material.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:18pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Assets and liabilities measured at fair value on a recurring basis</p><ix:nonNumeric id="F_000422" name="us-gaap:ScheduleOfFairValueAssetsAndLiabilitiesMeasuredOnRecurringBasisTableTextBlock" contextRef="C_0001667161_20200101_20201231" escape="true" continuedAt="F_000422_cnt_1">
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.54%;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Assets and liabilities measured at fair value on a recurring basis are summarized below.&#160;&#160;&#160;.</p></ix:nonNumeric><ix:continuation id="F_000422_cnt_1">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#160;</p>
